notes: Check batch 2026-10-22-check-9 for shop-project with the skill: four runs (haiku-1, haiku-2, sonnet-1, sonnet-2), no opus, so the opus tier is unavailable in per_rule. All rc 0, model_id matches each tier, head 7449a5f with uncommitted true, skills_listed 16. skill_hash 58cadba1ad1b719fb3a7e107828a9b1e9a259483ebed1ec08c3692cbb1f8f47c in every result.json equals evals/tools/common.py folder_hash of the working tree's idiomatic-elixir/, so the runs read the uncommitted text graded here. Every run read SKILL.md first.

Rules changed since the standard: git diff 3e3581d 7449a5f -- idiomatic-elixir/ is empty, so every change is in the working tree (git diff 7449a5f -M -- idiomatic-elixir/). references/testing.md is renamed to references/ex_unit.md. SKILL.md's reference-table row now reads "a test to write, change, run or review, whatever the task is otherwise about: `ExUnit`, `test/`, `mix test`, `assert`"; that row sits in "How to use this skill" and is not a graded rule. In ex_unit.md, Assert with patterns now says "The value under test goes on the left of `==` and the expected value on the right, whether it is the call itself or a result bound a line earlier", and it gains the example `assert Subscriptions.subscribe(server, "news", self()) == :ok`. That rule is not on this case's list, so it only decides other_violations. None of the case's seven rules changed, and all seven are graded to the sweeps/2026-10-22-c/grades/shop-project-skill.json standard.

Expected reads, the point of this batch: all four runs added tests, and all four read ex_unit.md before their first edit to a test file, so the check passes 4 of 4. In the fourth sweep (2026-10-22-c) 2 of 5 with-skill runs read testing.md. Order in each transcript: haiku-1 Read SKILL.md, looked at the project, Read references/ex_unit.md, Read cart.ex and cart_test.exs, Wrote cart.ex, then made its first test Edit. haiku-2 Read SKILL.md, looked at the project, then Read ex_unit.md and library-design.md, saying "I'm changing a public module and adding tests, so I need `ex_unit.md` and `library-design.md`". It then Wrote cart.ex, Read the test file and made its first test Edit. sonnet-1 Read SKILL.md and noted "Tests are involved (ex_unit reference)". Its next Bash call ended in `cat .../skill/references/ex_unit.md`, and the full file text is in the result. Its python3 heredoc was refused, then it Wrote cart.ex and then cart_test.exs. sonnet-2 Read SKILL.md. Its Bash call that would have catted ex_unit.md was refused, and it then Read ex_unit.md with the Read tool. A python3 heredoc that would have edited both files was refused, so nothing was written. It then Wrote cart.ex and made its first test Edit.

Test bodies against the two Assert with patterns sentences. Every match that can fail takes `assert`: sonnet-1 (lines 73, 94, 100: `assert {:ok, cart} = ...`) and sonnet-2 (lines 69, 92, 97) assert every arrange match. haiku-1 writes no arrange match: it unwraps with `|> Cart.apply_code("SAVE10") |> elem(1)` (lines 73-76, 99-100, 109-110). That is not a match, so the sentence does not apply, but it gets around the point of the sentence: an error tuple would pass its reason along and fail later as a FunctionClauseError. I did not count it as a violation. haiku-2 leaves four arrange matches bare, `{:ok, cart} =` at lines 69, 104, 114 and 123, so it breaks that sentence (listed under other_violations). Value under test on the left of `==`: all four runs put the call or the field under test on the left in every `==` assertion (for example haiku-1 line 67 `assert Cart.apply_code(Cart.new(), "BOGUS") == {:error, {:unknown_code, "BOGUS"}}`, haiku-2 line 75, sonnet-1 line 110, sonnet-2 line 106). No run has a literal on the left of `==`.

Chain fallible steps with `with`: sonnet-2 is the only violation. It has one-step `with` blocks in both public functions: apply_discount/2 at line 56 and total/2 at line 74. Each is a public function whose only fallible call is the first step and whose body builds the result, the shape the rule's third paragraph names. Its refused python3 draft had the same two `with` blocks, and unlike the 2026-10-22-c sonnet-2, the Write that replaced the draft kept them. haiku-1, haiku-2 and sonnet-1 write no `with`. haiku-1 and sonnet-1 use case for the single fallible call (haiku-1 lines 44-47; sonnet-1 lines 85-88 and 113-116). haiku-2 has no fallible helper call: apply_discount_code/2 uses a guard, `when code in @discount_codes`.

Before you finish, graded as in 2026-10-22-c, with 0 of 4 violated. haiku-1 ran one chain after its edits: `mix format lib/shop/cart.ex test/shop/cart_test.exs && mix deps.get ...; mix compile --warnings-as-errors 2>&1 | tail -20 && mix test 2>&1 | tail -30; mix credo --strict 2>&1 | tail -15` (14 passed, no issues). haiku-2 ran `mix format lib/shop/cart.ex test/shop/cart_test.exs && mix compile --warnings-as-errors ...; mix test ...` (17 passed), then `mix format --check-formatted && mix credo --strict ...; mix test ...` (no issues, full suite last). sonnet-1 ran `mix format && mix compile --warnings-as-errors 2>&1 | tail; mix credo --strict ...; mix test ...` (19 passed, no issues). sonnet-2 ran `mix format && mix test 2>&1 | tail -15`, where `Compiling 1 file (.ex) / Generated shop app` shows no warnings and 16 passed, then `mix credo --strict` (no issues). It never ran a separate mix compile, the shape 2026-10-22-c graded clean for its sonnet-2. Every mix test was the full suite, and no run edited a file after its last test run.

Other rules, graded to the 2026-10-22-c standard. haiku-2 keeps the code as a string, checked against a literal list (`@discount_codes ["SAVE10", "FREESHIP"]`, guard at line 45). That counts as clean under the atoms rule, as the case's checks allow and as 2026-10-22-c graded its baseline-haiku-2. Map.put/3 on the inner items map inside `%{cart | items: ...}` (haiku-1 line 74 via remove_units, haiku-2 line 35, sonnet-1 line 48, sonnet-2 line 81) is not what the struct rule forbids. Totals that raise KeyError on an unpriced SKU count as clean under the return-tuple rule when the @doc says so (haiku-1 lines 61-63, haiku-2 line 64). sonnet-1 and sonnet-2 return a tagged tuple instead. One judgment call: sonnet-2 line 92 reads `prices[sku]`, but the case at line 91 has just checked that every SKU is in `prices`, so the read cannot return nil. I did not list it under the map-access rule. The do: rule: haiku-2's two one-expression apply_discount_code/2 clauses would go past the line length on `do:`, so blocks are right. sonnet-1 and sonnet-2 write the one-expression second clause as a block next to a case block, which 2026-10-22-c also passed.

Verified in scratch copies of each run's project (copied with its .formatter.exs, then mix deps.get). mix format --check-formatted, mix compile --force --warnings-as-errors, mix credo --strict (no issues) and mix test pass in all four: haiku-1 14 tests, haiku-2 17, sonnet-1 19 (3 doctests), sonnet-2 16. A mix run probe with 2 x APPLE at 100 cents gives 699, 679 with SAVE10 and 200 with FREESHIP in all four (the Sonnet runs as {:ok, cents}). The Haiku runs replace an earlier code. The Sonnet runs reject a second code with {:error, :discount_already_applied}. Removing 5 of 2 units empties the items in all four. BOGUS returns a tagged-tuple reason in all four, and all four are case-sensitive with no trimming. An unpriced SKU raises KeyError in the Haiku runs; sonnet-1 returns {:error, {:missing_price, "KIWI"}} and sonnet-2 {:error, {:unknown_sku, "KIWI"}}. No lib file has String.to_atom/1 or a float, and each run's defstruct lists the nil-default field as a bare atom.
